items.text: While we're all debating whether AI will lead to a bad outcome for humanity, it's important to remember that most of the world hasn’t even started using it yet. Pedro, Brex’s CEO, likes to refer to a specific chart (see the clip): “Each dot is 3.2 million people. Every gray box is someone that never used AI in the world (84%). Green boxes are free chatbot users (16%). Orange boxes are people who pay $20 a month for AI (~0.3%). And this tiny red box is people using agents effectively (~0.04%).” I think the chart is from February 2026, so things have probably picked up since then, but we're still super early. 📌 Watch the full episode here: https://t.co/0E7XHvBEBR

items.title: There are two ways AI progress could go very badly and that we must avoid
items.text: There are two ways AI progress could go very badly and that we must avoid. First, we could lose control of the future to AI. This is unacceptable; we are unapologetically on Team Humanity, and AI must always serve people. To ensure that, we need ways to ensure that alignment and safety techniques stay ahead of progress in model capabilities. Second, we could end up in a world with too much concentration of power. If an extraordinarily powerful AI is used by one person or company to impress their worldview onto everyone else, the results could be extremely dystopian.
